# Exercise guidance — coverage checklist, asset manifest and production brief

## The honest headline

**The animations in this app are original vector diagrams generated by the parametric figure
engine in `figure.js`. They have not been reviewed by a qualified strength coach or
physiotherapist. They are not demonstration video and must not be treated as verified
technique.** The app says this on every exercise detail screen.

No third-party media is used. No media URLs are invented. Nothing is labelled as reviewed.

## Coverage checklist

| Requirement | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| All 35 original exercise entries covered | **Done** | Expanded to 40 variants |
| Combined movements split into variants | **Done** | pulldown / pull-up / assisted / weighted; conventional / trap-bar deadlift; bodyweight / weighted leg raise; kneeling / standing ab wheel |
| Each variant has its own performance history | **Done** | Keyed by `variantId`; verified by test |
| Each variant has a distinct animation | **Done** | 41 animations, zero shared between variants (verified programmatically) |
| Start and finish positions | **Done** | Every animation is a pose pair, eased between |
| Identifiable equipment in the figure | **Partial** | Barbell (plate end-on), back-racked bar, dumbbells, cable/band line, bench, landmine. Machines are drawn as a bench/pad abstraction |
| Controllable animation | **Done** | Pause/play on the detail sheet |
| Reduced-motion stills | **Done** | Honours the OS setting and an in-app override; renders the start pose |
| Text alternative | **Done** | Every exercise has a `direction` sentence plus full written cues |
| Movement direction | **Done** | `direction` field |
| Muscle groups | **Done** | `primary` + `secondary` |
| Setup / execution / breathing cues | **Done** | Every variant. **Unreviewed** |
| Common mistakes | **Done** | 3 per variant typical |
| Equipment alternatives | **Done** | 2–3 per variant, all resolving to real variants |
| Previous / today's target / why | **Done** | On the card and in the detail sheet |
| Feedback wired to planning | **Done** | Feedback → engine → next prescription, with the effect shown immediately |
| Offline | **Done** | Animations are code, not media. Nothing to download, nothing to fail |
| Usable when media fails | **Done** | The figure is decorative; all guidance is text |
| **Reviewed demonstration video** | **NOT DONE — gap** | See the production brief below |
| **Qualified review of cue text** | **NOT DONE — gap** | See below |

## Asset manifest

Generated at runtime as `ASSET_MANIFEST` in `exercises.js`. Every entry carries:

```
exercise, animation (lifts.js key), type, licence, reviewed:false,
reviewer:null, status:'unreviewed-original', textAlternative:true, cueSource
```

- **Source:** original parametric SVG, generated by `figure.js` from pose definitions in
  `lifts.js` / `stretches.js`. Written for this project.
- **Licence:** original work, owned by the app owner. No third-party assets, no stock media,
  no scraped imagery.
- **Review status:** `unreviewed-original` for all 41 animations and all cue text.
- **Reviewer:** none.

## Known gaps in the current assets

1. No filmed demonstration for any exercise.
2. Figures are 2D side-view. Grip width, foot angle, bar path nuance and frontal-plane
   movement are not represented.
3. Movements that live in the frontal plane (lateral raise, face pull) are approximated from
   the side, where they read similarly to a front raise.
4. No per-side view for rotation work (landmine rotation, Pallof press).
5. Machine exercises use a generic bench/pad abstraction rather than a recognisable machine.
6. **No cue text has been reviewed by a qualified professional.** The cues are written from
   general training practice. Some are consensus; some are judgement.

## Production brief — what a real asset set needs

For whoever films this properly.

**Scope.** 40 variants. Two angles each (side and 45° front). 6–8 seconds per angle, looping
cleanly, no music, no talking.

**Per exercise, deliver:**
- 1080×1350 (4:5) and 1080×1080, H.264 MP4, under 2 MB each after compression, plus a WebP
  still of the start position and one of the finish position.
- A 3-frame sprite (start / mid / finish) for the reduced-motion and offline fallback.
- Shot on a plain mid-grey background, even lighting, no logos, no branded apparel.

**Technique sign-off.** Each movement reviewed and signed by an accredited S&C coach (ASCA
Level 2 or equivalent in Australia) before anything is marked `reviewed: true`. The manifest
has `reviewer` and `reviewed` fields waiting for exactly this. Record the reviewer's name,
credential and date.

**Cue review.** The same reviewer should sign off the setup, execution, breathing and mistakes
text. Anything they will not sign gets deleted rather than softened.

**Separately, for the pain pathway:** the severity cut-off that pauses an exercise (currently
5 out of 10) is a developer's safety-biased guess and should be reviewed by a physiotherapist,
or replaced with "any pain pauses it" if that is the safer default.

**Until that review exists**, the app continues to label every animation as a diagram and to
state that it does not diagnose injuries or prescribe rehabilitation. Do not flip
`reviewed: true` without the signature.
